name: watch-coordinator-infra-classification
title: Watch coordinator cannot distinguish an infrastructure CI failure from a real one
description: sd-ship Stage 3's watch coordinator reports settled-blocked for both a genuine check failure and a GitHub-side infrastructure failure, so a run cannot tell a retry-worthy blocker from one that no retry will clear. Give the coordinator an infrastructure classification, or document that the operator must inspect job steps before deciding.
creator: sdelmas
notes: Deferred once by the operator on 2026-08-06 when the sibling fixes shipped in PR #156; tasked rather than dropped. The coordinator's outcome vocabulary is fixed at settled-green, settled-blocked, timed-out, and probe-failed (watch-coordinator.md:58-65) with no infrastructure category. Note that watch-coordinator.md is installed from the sd-ai-command-pack (.sd-ai-command-pack/manifest.json), so changing the coordinator itself is an upstream change; only the operator-facing guidance is editable in this repository. Sequencing: ten active tasks edit .trellis/spec/backend/quality-guidelines.md. Cluster membership is decided by the PRD's stated deliverable -- a Requirement or acceptance criterion that writes to that file -- not by whether implement.jsonl lists it, since the manifest is a read-for-context list and several non-cluster tasks cite the file as a contract to read. `order` 10 within the P3 band encodes the intended landing sequence (Review And Retry Conventions; adjacent to the review cluster). Tasks with no `order` sort as 0 and therefore run before this cluster, which is intended: they do not contend for this file.
